metaDescription: Six 50 pint dehumidifiers with built-in pumps compared on lift height, hose length, serviceable pumps, noise and efficiency for basements.
expertTake: The GE with a 15 foot lift and a 16 foot hose is the pick for most below-grade basements. The Midea pump model is the value-minded choice if you want a quiet low mode and Energy Star. Skip a pump unit if you have a floor drain beside the machine, because a plain hose model has one fewer part to fail.
introParagraphs: A pump changes what a dehumidifier can do. Instead of relying on gravity, the machine collects water in a small reservoir and pushes it up a tube to a sink, a stand pipe or a window, which frees you from carrying a bucket up the stairs every day.

The pump is also the part most likely to cause trouble. Lift height, hose length, whether the pump can be cleaned, and how much noise it makes when it fires are the details that separate a convenient machine from a nuisance.

products.name: GE 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump and 16 ft Hose
products.description:
The GE pairs a plain, well-understood compressor with a built-in pump that the listing says moves water up to 15 feet, and it ships with a 16 foot hose. That combination solves the below-grade basement problem, where the drain, sink or window is higher than the floor. Smart Dry then raises the fan speed when the air is wet and lowers it once the room settles.

The pump is the reason to pick it over the same maker's non-pump model. A pump adds cost and one more moving part, but you get a hose long enough to reach a utility sink across the room. Compared with the Midea pump unit, the GE has a larger coverage claim and a longer included hose, and sits in a higher price tier.

Owners should flush the line each season and keep the hose from kinking. Because it is a major brand, filters and service are easy to find, which matters in year three. Plan the install before you buy: run the hose along the wall rather than across the floor, secure it so it cannot kink, and test the pump with a bucket of water before leaving it alone for a week. A well-set line can run for years with only a seasonal rinse, and a poorly routed one is the usual cause of an overflow.
products.bestFor: Below-grade basements where the drain sits well above the floor.
pros: 15 ft vertical lift with a 16 ft hose
Smart Dry fan speed saves energy

products.name: Midea 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump 4,500 sq ft
products.description:
This Midea uses a built-in pump that drains vertically or horizontally into a sink or out of a window. The low mode is listed at 49 dBA, quiet enough for a finished basement, and the humidity target adjusts from 35 percent. Energy Star certification keeps running cost reasonable.

It is the sensible choice for a finished space where you want to hear the TV over the machine. Against the GE, it gives up some coverage and the long hose, but it sits lower in price tier.

Pump noise is worth testing at install, and the line should be flushed each season. Wash the filter monthly. The ability to drain into a window is useful in a walk-out basement, but it needs a stable line so that wind and gravity do not push water back. Treat the low-mode noise as the one you will live with, since the pump will add its own brief hum whenever it cycles.
products.bestFor: Finished basements that need pump drainage and a quiet low mode.
cons: Smaller coverage claim than the GE
Shorter reach than the 16 ft hose model

products.name: DuraComfort 50 Pint DOE Dehumidifier with Pump
products.description:
DuraComfort stands out for stating its rating as 50 pints DOE, which means the current US test, alongside a much larger 119 pint figure at a hot test point. The honest number is the 50, and it is stated openly. The pump pushes water up to 16.4 feet, the highest lift in the guide.

You can switch between the pump, a gravity hose and the tank, which makes it flexible for a house where the drain may change. Compared with the GE, it offers a bit more lift but a lesser-known brand and a mid price tier.

Flush the pump line each season and register the warranty. The three drain choices mean you can start with the pump and fall back to gravity if you later add a floor drain. Because the brand is less established, keep the receipt and the manual, and note the filter size so you can reorder.
products.bestFor: Basements with a high drain and a buyer who wants an honest DOE number.
pros: 16.4 ft lift is the highest here

products.name: hOmeLabs 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump and Wi-Fi
products.description:
The hOmeLabs states 50 pints at 80F and claims 7,500 square feet, the largest claim in the lineup. Wi-Fi lets you adjust the settings from anywhere, and the integrated pump allows continuous drainage. The much larger 120 pint figure is a hot-lab number.

The coverage claim is generous, so treat it as an upper bound. It sits near the top of the price tier, similar to the GE.

In year three, keep the pump line clean and the filter washed. The Wi-Fi app can alert you to a full tank or a humidity spike, which is helpful in a vacation house. Remember that cloud features are a convenience, so confirm the front-panel controls work on their own.
products.bestFor: Large open basements that benefit from app control.
pros: Largest coverage claim at 7,500 sq ft

products.name: Hisense 50 Pint Lift-Up Dehumidifier with Pump
products.description:
Hisense bundles the pump with a quick-connect hose that routes water to a drain. The unit offers three modes and three fan speeds. It is portable, with a lift-up design.

The sibling non-pump Hisense lists operation down to 38F, which suggests similar low-temperature engineering, but check the listing for this exact model. It sits mid-high in price tier.

Flush the line and wash the filter on schedule. Quick-connect fittings save time during cleaning, because you can detach the hose without a tool. Do not rely on a fitting alone for a long vertical run, and support the line with a clip near the top. Its three fan speeds let you trade a little noise for faster drying after a wet week, then drop back to low once the room settles.
products.bestFor: Cooler basements where a quick-connect hose and fan control help.
pros: Three modes and three fan speeds
cons: Confirm the cold limit for this model

products.name: Whirlpool 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump
products.description:
Whirlpool adds caster wheels and top carry handles, which matters because a 50 pint machine is heavy. Electronic controls and an adjustable humidistat keep the interface simple. A built-in pump handles drainage.

It is the highest price tier in the lineup, so you are paying for brand and mobility. For a machine that stays put, the GE or Midea offers more per tier.

Care is routine: filter, tank and pump line. Casters are handy when you move the machine to wash a filter or to dry a different room, but they also tempt people to drag it across a wet floor. Lift the front edge when crossing thresholds and keep the pump line detached while moving.
products.bestFor: Homes where the machine moves between rooms or floors.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The GE lists a 15 foot lift and a 16 foot hose, while the DuraComfort lists 16.4 feet. Measure the vertical distance from the unit to the drain and add a margin. A pump that barely reaches struggles and clogs. As a rule, add two feet to your measured rise to cover bends and sag, because a pump that is asked to work at its maximum lift tends to be slower and noisier. Always measure first.

Pumps clog with slime in damp basements. Some brands bury the pump, while others make it removable. Look for a design that lets you flush the line each season. Ask whether the pump can be flushed without disassembly, because a sealed pump cannot be cleaned and becomes the first thing to fail.

A pump adds a buzz when it runs. The Midea lists 49 dBA on low. In a finished basement, check owner feedback on pump noise. If you plan to place the unit near a bedroom wall, the pump buzz matters more than the compressor hum.

The DuraComfort states DOE, the hOmeLabs 80F, and both quote bigger hot-lab figures. The 2019 test is 65F and 60 percent. Plan on the lower number. A hot-lab figure like 120 pints is useful only as a reminder to read the small print.

The hOmeLabs claims 7,500 square feet and the GE 5,000. Claims assume a mild problem. A wet basement needs one size up. For a damp cellar, subtract a margin from the claim and choose the next size up if you can see standing moisture.

A 50 pint machine draws roughly 500 to 800 watts. Energy Star on the Midea and Whirlpool keeps costs down. Running cost is roughly proportional to hours run, so a pump unit that finishes the job sooner pays back.

specDecoder.meaning: How high the pump can push water vertically. Measure your own run before trusting a listing, since bends and sag cost lift.
specDecoder.watchFor: The GE lists 15 ft and the DuraComfort 16.4 ft.

specDecoder.meaning: The US test at 65F and 60 percent humidity since 2019. This is the figure to plan around when comparing units.
A larger figure at 95F and 90 percent humidity. It is a marketing peak, so ignore it when sizing.
Sound level. Every 10 dBA sounds about twice as loud. Quiet low mode matters most for finished spaces.
Fan logic that adapts to humidity. It also lowers the energy used per pint.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pump performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated lift and hose length. The GE and DuraComfort led. Lift is only useful if the hose is long enough to use it. Reaching the drain is the point of buying a pump.

howWeEvaluated.title: Serviceability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for removable pumps and clear service routes. Where a pump is buried inside the case, we treated it as harder to maintain. A pump that can be cleaned earns extra credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We read decibel claims such as the Midea at 49 dBA. Pump noise was inferred from published low-mode figures and owner feedback patterns. Finished spaces need a quiet low mode.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored DOE-stated ratings over hot-lab peaks. A stated DOE rating beats a hot-lab figure for planning. We discounted peaks printed at hot test points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered brand support and owner feedback patterns. Brand reach decides how easy it is to find a filter in year four. Service reach decides long-term cost.

cards.label: Pump
cards.text: Needed when the drain is above the unit. The GE and DuraComfort reach furthest.

cards.label: Gravity
cards.text: Simpler when the drain is below. Choose a non-pump 50 pint unit then.

howToChoose.note: If a floor drain is nearby, skip the pump.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A pump with enough lift, a serviceable line and a rating you trust.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GE and DuraComfort are the strongest pump choices.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The drain is far or high. The GE earns it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The drain is near. The Midea suffices.

maintenance.why: Algae clogs tubes and strains pumps. Do this after any long shutdown and before the damp season.
A clogged filter frosts the coil. Dry it fully before refitting to prevent mildew.
Slime builds up. Replace the tube if it clouds or stiffens.
Dust blocks heat transfer. Use a soft brush and unplug the machine first.
Sensors drift. Compare the reading to a separate meter.

faq.q: How high can a dehumidifier pump lift?
faq.a: Listings range from 15 to 16.4 feet vertically. Measure your run. Measure both the vertical rise and the horizontal run, since both reduce flow. Check that the unit includes the hose you need.
Prices range from a mid tier to a premium tier. Check the listing. Premium tiers pay for brand, lift and control features, not for more pints. Look at lift, hose length and serviceability together.
Some models allow it. Check before buying. Pumps that cannot be reached are the main reason units are replaced early. Drain the tank and line before storing the unit.
Compressor units last 5 to 10 years. Most 50 pint units serve basements up to about 4,500 square feet if the problem is moderate. Cold rooms reduce output on every compressor model.
For most basements up to 4,500 square feet, yes. A hose to a nearby drain removes the pump as a failure point. Test the pump with water before leaving it alone.
Aim for 40 to 50 percent. A hygrometer is the only way to know the room is where you set it. Hold the target on cool nights too.
